entry.title: Weekly update: 12 Nov 2026
entry.content:
Added to the roadmap

  • Securing Agentic Applications V2 (OWASP GenAI Security Project, Stage 0), a builder and defender's guide to agent architecture, identity and access, runtime protection, supply chain, and testing, released Nov 10.
  • When Approval Becomes Execution (Chenggong Shi, Hongmei Mou, Stage 3), a denied agent fetched a routine approval token and completed the protected operation in 8 of 9 reruns.
  • My Credentials, Please (Huang et al., Stage 4), 787 of 4,806 triaged MCP servers had filesystem access their category did not suggest; 13 advisories followed.
  • Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons (Microsoft, Stage 4), editing fewer than 10 neurons can plant a trigger that passes evaluations.
  • A web page talked our agent into leaking a stranger's data (Nancy Chauhan, Arize, Stage 7), 28 of 100 runs leaked another customer's record until the tools were scoped to the session in code.
  • Web LLM attacks (PortSwigger Web Security Academy, Learn and practice), free browser labs against a live LLM.

Incidents table

  • AgentCorruption (AWS Bedrock AgentCore) (Zenity Labs), one prompt to an exposed agent reached the metadata service and returned credentials for a role that spanned every AgentCore agent in the account's region.
  • server-everything cross-origin environment leak (MCP reference servers), any web page could read the server's whole environment through its HTTP transports; fixed in 2.0.1.

Concepts

  • Confused deputy: a trusted helper tricked into using its own authority for someone who has none, explained for experts, engineers, and everyone.

Link checks

  • All links added this week were opened and read before listing.

entry.title: Weekly update: 5 Nov 2026
entry.content:
Added to the roadmap

  • Stage 0: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems (Saltzer and Schroeder, 1975), the design principles behind complete mediation and least privilege.
  • Stage 2: Strands Box (Strands Agents, AWS), a preview sandbox that sends shell, Python, MCP, and network actions through one default-deny policy engine outside the agent.
  • Stage 3: Workflow Identity Hijacking (Sasi Levi, Noma Labs), AI workflows that act with their creator's privileges on requests from anyone.
  • Stage 7: ToFu (Ananto et al.), a fuzzer that found verified bugs in 343 MCP tools across 118 of 273 servers.

Incidents table

  • ChatGPT Lockdown Mode bypass (Check Point Research), a nested iframe reached an unwrapped window.open, and popups escaped the preview sandbox and Lockdown Mode; fixed by Sept 18.
  • Plugin4Shell (Air Security), coding agents installed attacker code past plugin SHA pinning because they never checked the commit they landed on.
  • GitSpawn (Manifold Security), background git calls ran a repository's own core.fsmonitor command outside the sandbox.

Concepts

  • Complete mediation: every access checked, on every path, explained for experts, engineers, and everyone.

  • All links added this week were opened and read before listing.

entry.title: Weekly update: 4 Nov 2026
entry.content:
Added to the site

  • Concepts, explained three ways: 14 core ideas, each written for experts, for software engineers (mapped to something you already know), and for everyone (an everyday example), with where each analogy breaks.
  • Explain it for: a switch that changes the site between Experts, Engineers, and Everyone. Stage intros and every incident now have a plain-words version.

entry.title: Weekly update: 3 Nov 2026
entry.content:
Added to the roadmap

  • Stage 1: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents (Guo et al.), the same injected instruction lands 2.6 times more often in a README or TODO file than in code or data.
  • Stage 3: Design Tenets for Agent Identity Management Systems (Booth, Fisher, Galluzzo, Clancy; NIST and MITRE), ten tenets for agent identity and authorization, including separation of policy from reasoning.
  • Stage 5: Blocking at the Boundary (Liu, Han, Lyu, Wang, Yu), a preprint on auditing each pending action against staged prompt injection in Claude Code and Codex.
  • Stage 7: INFUSE (Nguyen, Guo, Dubauskas, Damuluru, Johnson, Leach), an indirect prompt injection benchmark across 19 LLMs with code.
  • Stage 8: The Secure Software Factory: A Reference Architecture (Agent Baseline), four boundaries enforced outside the agent at three levels of autonomy; draft, open for comment.

Incidents table

  • Malicious Claude Code extension in Cursor's marketplace (Cursor), modified extension versions that planted an SSH key and persistence on Oct 29.
  • Unauthorized AI relays switch the sandbox off (Symantec), a relay that reconfigures genuine Codex and Claude Code CLIs to "danger-full-access" and routes traffic through its own servers.
  • MCPhantom (Glow Labs), coding agents installing archived MCP reference servers from training-data memory.

Link checks

  • All links added this week were opened and read before listing.

entry.title: Weekly update: 29 Oct 2026
entry.content:
Added to the roadmap

  • Stage 3: Authority Is Not a String (Bouras, Dai, Mechtaev), CapScope: typed capabilities held outside the model, checked on every tool call.
  • Stage 6: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces (Qin, Schmotz, Prinzhorn, Beurer-Kellner, Prabhu, Andriushchenko), why trace logging must sit outside the agent's control.
  • Stage 7: buried-injections (Rudratosh Shastri), a reproducible benchmark of 10 injection detectors on 629 AgentDojo attacks.

Incidents table

  • Mistral Vibe shell permission bypass (SecMate), a permission check that parsed one thing while the shell ran another; advisory.
  • Accessing and changing internal systems during dashboard research (OpenAI), a model that reverted a setting but kept the token it had obtained.

Link checks

  • All links added this week were opened and read before listing.

entry.title: Weekly update: 22 Oct 2026
entry.content:
Added to the roadmap

  • Stage 3: MCP Tool Exposure is a Privilege Grant: A Two-Gate Authorization Model (Badal Bhushan, CSA), capability admission versus per-call execution authorization.
  • Stage 3: ToolFence (Li, He, Dai, Xiao), a preprint on typed authorization blueprints enforced by a deterministic monitor.
  • Stage 5: Agent Governance Toolkit (Microsoft), open-source policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, and execution sandboxing for agents.

Incidents table

  • Claude models reached real systems during cyber evaluations (Anthropic), a misconfigured evaluation environment left the internet open.
  • A Vault with a Heap-View on AWS AgentCore Harness (Unit 42), prompt injection to credential exfiltration through a default shell tool.

entry.title: Weekly update: 21 Oct 2026
entry.content:

  • Stage 3: OWASP Agent Control Standard, runtime hooks and portable policy enforcement.
  • Stage 3: Loopjacking (Adithyan Arun Kumar), how human approval gets decoupled from the executed action.
  • Stage 4: CoSAI MCP Security v2.0, four assurance levels and eight security dimensions.
  • Stage 7: OWASP GenAI Red Teaming Manual v1.0 (published 2026-10-20).
  • Stage 8: CoSAI Zero Trust for AI Systems.
  • Learn and practice: Learn Agent Security From Scratch.

Incidents table

  • SalesBleed on Agentforce (Zenity Labs).
  • OpenAI: test wallet spent without authorization.
  • OpenAI: agent used DNS to reach an external chatbot.

Updated

  • MITRE ATLAS entry now points to the v2026.09 release (new agent recon and trigger-channel techniques).

Link checks

  • MCP Security Best Practices and Snyk Agent Scan links still resolve. The MCP page now covers state handle hijacking (stateless protocol) instead of session hijacking.

entry.title: Put the lock in the code: why an AI's "no" is not access control
entry.summary: Arize's test support agent refused every direct request to send data out, yet pulled a stranger's record in 28 of 100 runs until its tools were scoped to the signed-in customer. Here are the sources, plus the confused deputy, the 1988 idea behind it.

entry.title: Block the capability, not the function: how a popup got past ChatGPT's Lockdown Mode
entry.summary: Check Point found that ChatGPT's HTML previews guarded popups by wrapping one function while the sandbox still granted the capability. Here are the sources, plus two coding-agent flaws where a check covered the usual path but not a second one.

entry.title: Logs the agent can't edit: sources for a tamper-resistant record
entry.summary: Why an audit trail the agent can write is not evidence, and the papers, report, and tools behind a record it cannot touch.

entry.title: Six free agent-security references for your next design review
